mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in nonfarm payrolls growth (PAYEMS) over two months, coinciding with a rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals labor market softening, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change falls by >0.5% and UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS decelerates by >0.5% and UNRATE rises in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output and reduced corporate revenue prospects, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) combined with falling real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a collapse in residential investment and consumer demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both fall month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both HOUST and GDPC1 decline in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of near-zero or negative federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25% for ≥6 months) in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of prolonged near-zero FEDFUNDS and low inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% for three consecutive months, regardless of other macro conditions, is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to deteriorating consumer demand and earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 7% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-over-month rebound in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) after two prior months of decline signals improving consumer confidence and spending, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 posts a month-over-month increase after two consecutive declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive following a GDPC1 rebound after two declines.
